glosses: Caused by an agent that enters the host's body (such as a bacterium, virus, parasite, or prion); often, also, transmitted among hosts via any of various routes (for example, contact, droplet-borne, airborne, waterborne, foodborne, fomite-borne, or bloodborne).

examples.text: Cancer is usually not infectious.
More infectious diseases like the flu are usually less potent.

glosses: Able to infect others; capable of transmitting pathogens.

examples.text: Despite feeling better, the patient is still infectious.
I doubt that [saliva] is very infectious ... I don't think this is a normal route of transmission.

glosses: Spreading quickly from one person to another.

examples.text: Her enthusiasm for work can be really infectious.
When Maisie first met Danny, she remembers that he had an infectious laugh and a love for music.

glosses: Memorable and invoking excitement or interest.

examples.text: Pop music is more infectious than elevator music.
